plan.topic: Finished your tirzepatide single-dose pen: how to dispose of it safely, per the Instructions for Use and FDA sharps guidance
plan.angle:
08:00 practical pen moment. Follow the task's length arm and hook archetype.

- **Sentence 1 (14 words or fewer):** 'Used tirzepatide pen in your hand? Here's where it should go.' Scene 1's on-screen text matches it.
- **By 6 s:** what the US single-dose pen IFU says about disposal, quoted only if the IFU URL loads. The pen is single-use; put it in a sharps container right after use.
- **FDA sharps guidance:** an FDA-cleared container, or the household-container option exactly as FDA prints it. Don't throw loose pens in the trash or put them in recycling. Follow your local rules.
- **Untagged line:** UK, Canada and Australia rules differ, so ask your pharmacy or local council where to drop off a full container.
- **Scope card:** 'US single-dose pen. KwikPens and vials have their own leaflets; check the one in your box.'
- **Leave out:** doses, missed-dose talk and technique beyond the IFU.
- **Closing:** 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.', then a line that loops back to sentence 1. No subscribe line and no 'link in the description'.
- **Post note:** related-video target is the Pen how-to video.

Finished your US Zepbound (tirzepatide) single-dose pen? The kitchen trash isn't the place for it.

Finished your US Zepbound (tirzepatide) single-dose pen and wondering what to do with it? Tossing it straight into the kitchen trash feels harmless — but it isn't.

It's single-use: right into an FDA-cleared sharps container as soon as you're done. No sharps container handy? In the UK, Canada or Australia, rules differ, so ask your pharmacy or local council where full containers go. POST NOTE (Exp G): set the related-video link to the Pen how-to long video. MUST DO BEFORE PUBLISH: open https://pi.lilly.com/us/zepbound-pen-us-ifu.pdf in a PDF viewer, copy the 'Revised' date printed at the end of the IFU (DD Mon YYYY) into src1's year field, and don't use the PI's 28 Aug 2026 date unless the IFU shows it. factcheck.summary: This Short passes, with three small fixes listed below. Its disposal advice matches the Zepbound single-dose pen instructions and the FDA's sharps-disposal page. The pen instructions say to put the used pen in an FDA-cleared sharps container right away, not to throw loose pens in household trash, and list the same five rules for a heavy-duty plastic household container as the script. I confirmed the text on the FDA page, including "about three-quarters (3/4) full, follow your community guidelines" and its "current as of 08/10/2023" date. I found the instructions' wording through Lilly-indexed search results, because the PDF itself wouldn't open as text. The script correctly says "3/4 full" comes from the FDA, not the pen instructions. The scope line (US single-dose pen only), the advice to ask locally outside the US and the "Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber." line are all there. There's no dosing, nothing about switching medicines and nothing harmful. One small wording issue: the pen instructions' "do not recycle" line is about the used sharps container, not loose pens.
